analysis.title: 2027 Treasury supply & debt limit outlook
key_insights: CACIB expects Treasury to hold coupon auction sizes unchanged near term and start raising issuance in H2 2027, mainly in the 2- to 7-year sector, with increases beginning in August 2027.
Gross coupon issuance is forecast to rise modestly to about USD4.5trn in 2027 from USD4.4trn in 2026. Net marketable borrowing is forecast at roughly USD2.1trn in 2027.
Long-end issuance is the key uncertainty. Treasury is weighing investor demand, market functioning and taxpayer cost. TIPS auction sizes are expected to stay broadly unchanged through 2027.
Net bill issuance is estimated at USD800-900bn in 2027 versus about USD721bn in FY2026. Bill supply should fall in December on tax receipts and rise again in January.

Bills are about USD7.4trn, or roughly 23% of marketable debt, below historical peaks. This leaves room to lean on bills, and any signal of a modestly shorter WAM would support longer-dated Treasuries by easing long-end supply.

Bill demand is supported by money market funds with nearly USD8trn in assets (government MMFs about USD6.6trn) and by Fed MBS reinvestment bill purchases of about USD14bn over the next four weeks. The Fed is not doing reserve management bill purchases in the coming four-week period.
Treasury debt is projected to hit the USD41.1trn statutory limit in early 2027, triggering extraordinary measures worth a few hundred USDbn.
The debt limit X-date is likely in Q4 2027, when extraordinary measures and the TGA are exhausted and markets begin pricing default risk.
Ahead of the X-date Treasury should cut bill issuance and draw down the TGA, which lifts bank reserves, and MMFs shift from bills to repo, pushing repo rates lower.
After Congress raises or suspends the limit, Treasury will rebuild the TGA through heavy bill issuance, draining reserves and redirecting MMF flows back to bills.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Modest rise from USD4.4trn in 2026, driven by 2- to 7-year increases from August 2027.
Bills play a larger role in deficit financing, with timing dependent on debt limit resolution.
Treasury projection, with the TGA expected to fall sharply in Q2 and Q3 2027 under the debt limit.
Limit expected to bind in early 2027, starting extraordinary measures.

risk_factors: Long-end coupon issuance decisions are uncertain and depend on demand and cost.
Debt limit negotiation timing and resolution could shift bill issuance and the X-date.
Default risk pricing as extraordinary measures and TGA are exhausted in Q4 2027.
Reserve drain after the TGA rebuild once the limit is raised or suspended.
Changes to Fed balance sheet policy and bill purchases.
